note: Primary documentation inspected for the event and interface choices of the three dossiers. Each receipt also captures, at run time, the host's own sysfs PMU description and the perf list entries of the events it used (events.json, environment.json).

linux_kernel_amd_pmu.running_kernel: 7.0.0-42-generic (Ubuntu); the upstream v7.0 source is assumed to match for these tables, and sysfs events/* on the running kernel (which the kernel derives from the same event map) agree with them
linux_kernel_amd_pmu.derived_fact: With nmi_watchdog=1 the hard-lockup detector holds one core counter, leaving five; every dossier group has five events and every measured row reported running == enabled (scheduling gate: full).

linux_perf_event_tables.tool: perf 7.0.14 (perf list -j --details); the amdzen3 pmu-events tables built into perf
linux_perf_event_tables.use: event names, encodings and descriptions; resolved per run and stored in each receipt's events.json

linux_man_pages.perf_event_open(2): pid == 0 and cpu == -1: 'This measures the calling process/thread on any CPU.'
linux_man_pages.sched_setaffinity(2): sched_getaffinity: 'If pid is zero, then the mask of the calling thread is returned.' (why the drivers snapshot the allowed set before pinning)
linux_man_pages.pthread_setaffinity_np(3): 'If the call is successful, and the thread is not currently running on one of the CPUs in cpuset, then it is migrated to one of those CPUs.'
linux_man_pages.pthread_attr_setaffinity_np(3): sets the affinity a created thread starts with
linux_man_pages.getrusage(2): RUSAGE_THREAD (since Linux 2.6.26) returns the calling thread's usage; ru_nivcsw counts involuntary context switches
linux_man_pages.sched_getcpu(3): the CPU the calling thread is running on, recorded at both ends of every window

amd_documentation.ppr_for_family_19h_model_50h: not obtained. A fetch attempt on 2026-10-31 returned only a web-viewer page, and no document number was verified to match this model. Event meanings are therefore taken only from the perf list descriptions and the kernel maps; no claim relies on PPR text.
amd_documentation.product_identification: AMD Ryzen 3 7330U, family 19h model 50h (lscpu: family 25, model 80), identified by AMD as Zen 3 (PMU_PROTOCOL.md cites AMD's product page)

host_clock.observation: The kernel log records 'Measured 3642704559 cycles TSC warp between CPUs, turning off TSC clock', 'Marking TSC unstable' and 'Switched to clocksource hpet'. Every clock read in these dossiers is therefore an HPET read through a system call (about 1.4 microseconds per read on this host), which raises the timing target to about 147 microseconds; HPET is one global counter, so timestamps from different CPUs are comparable.
